 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e128412c1947498fcc66fc86001b1910ae42649b857ae618507bd45376a61a68.png]
solution:
The correct answer is __NOR GATE**(Option 3)**.__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• NOR Gate__ is a universal logic gate.
 
• A __NOR Gate__ produces an output that is true only when all inputs are false.
 
• In Boolean algebra, the NOR gate is expressed as (A + B)'.
 
• The NOR gate is a combination of an OR Gate followed by a NOT Gate.
 
• It is commonly used in digital circuits due to its versatility in implementing any Boolean function.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **NAND Gate:**
 
 
• The output of a NAND gate is true when at least one of the inputs is false.
 
• It is also a universal gate and can be used to implement any Boolean function.
 
 
 
• **OR Gate:**
 
 
• The output of an OR gate is true when at least one input is true.
 
• It is represented by the Boolean expression A + B.
 
 
 
• **AND Gate:**
 
 
• The output of an AND gate is true only when all inputs are true.
 
• It is represented by the Boolean expression A.B.
